record.original_question: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its maximal immediate extensions? This is asked after observing that a particular extension (L,v) of F_p((t)) fails this existential-closedness property and, by a theorem cited in the paper, is therefore not extremal.

not all images of additive polynomials have the optimal approximation property ...
This gives rise to the following

Open problem 13: Is every extremal valued field existentially closed in its max

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (K, v) be a valued field, with value group vK and residue field Kv. Recall the following definitions.

(1) An extension (L, v) ⊇ (K, v) is called immediate if vL = vK and Lv = Kv. A valued field (K, v) is called maximal if it admits no proper immediate extension; every valued field has at least one maximal immediate extension.

(2) (K, v) is existentially closed in an extension (L, v) (in the language of valued fields) if every existential first-order formula with parameters from K that has a solution in L already has a solution in K.

(3) For a polynomial f ∈ K[X_1, …, X_n], let f(O_K^n) ⊆ K denote the image of the valuation ring O_K^n under f. The set f(O_K^n) is said to have the optimal approximation property if the supremum sup{v(a) : a ∈ f(O_K^n)} ∈ vK ∪ {∞} is attained by some element of f(O_K^n). The valued field (K, v) is called extremal if for every n ≥ 1 and every f ∈ K[X_1, …, X_n], the set f(O_K^n) has the optimal approximation property.

Question: Is every extremal valued field (K, v) existentially closed in each of its maximal immediate extensions?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a December 2025 survey on the model theory of tame valued fields. Related literature (notes on extremal and tame valued fields, characterization of extremal valued fields) discusses partial results — e.g., existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions implies henselian and defectless — but no source found resolves the implication from extremality to existential closedness in maximal immediate extensions.
